body.statement: For every two-sided pathwise-interior \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the outcome-score restrictions \(E_P(k\mid Y,J=j,X)=0\) are equivalent, cellwise, to \(B^{\mathsf T}k=0\).  The operator \(N=N_B=I_{K^2}-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^+B^{\mathsf T}\) is their pointwise \(D\)-orthogonal projector, \(b_{f_0}(X)\in\operatorname{range}\{G(X)\}\), and \(Qf_0=N_Bf_0-h^{\mathsf T}G(X)^+b_{f_0}(X)\) is the \(L^2(P)\)-orthogonal projection onto \(\mathcal T^\perp\) for every \(f_0\in L^2(P)\).
body.justification: The theorem eliminates the infinite continuous-outcome nuisance pointwise and leaves only one finite conditional Gram solve.
body.gap: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen use an equal-width outcome partition and nuisance-dependent conditional-probability functions for the binary continuous-outcome projection; no located source gives this exact multilevel \(K^{2}\)-cell plus \(2K^{2}\)-Gram representation.
body.consumer: It makes exact efficiency computation feasible without selecting an outcome sieve in the continuous birth-weight application.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \((y,x)\) outside the relevant null set and represent an observed-cell function by \(k=(k_{az})\in\mathbb R^{K^2}\).  Conditional independence gives
\[
E\{k(O)\mid Y=y,J=j,X=x\}
=\sum_{a,z}M_A(x)_{aj}M_Z(x)_{zj}k_{az}=B_{\cdot j}(x)^{\mathsf T}k. \tag{26}
\]
Thus all outcome-factor restrictions are exactly \(B^{\mathsf T}k=0\).  Lemma 3A proves that \(N_B\) is idempotent, \(D\)-self-adjoint, and has range \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\); it is consequently the pointwise \(D\)-orthogonal projector onto those restrictions.  Moreover \(R\mathbf 1_K=\mathbf 1_{K^2}\), so constants across cells are in \(\ker N_B\).  It follows that \(N_Bf_0\) has conditional mean zero given \((Y,X)\).

For a coordinate \(r=(j,a)\), posterior Bayes identity and iterated expectation give
\[
E\{kR_{\cdot j}\mathbf 1(A=a)\mid X\}
=E\{k\mathbf 1(J=j)\mathbf 1(A=a)\mid X\}
=\pi_jE\{k\mathbf 1(A=a)\mid J=j,X\}. \tag{27}
\]
The same equation holds with \(Z=z\).  Because \(\pi_j\geq\varepsilon\), the remaining measurement restrictions in Theorem 2 are exactly \(E(kc_r\mid X)=0\) for all \(r\).  When \(k=N_Bk\), conditional \(D\)-self-adjointness gives
\[
E(kc_r\mid X)=E\{k(N_Bc_r)\mid X\}=E(kh_r\mid X). \tag{28}
\]

If \(v\in\ker G(X)\), then
\[
0=v^{\mathsf T}Gv=E\{(v^{\mathsf T}h)^2\mid X\},
\]
so \(v^{\mathsf T}h=0\) conditionally and \(v^{\mathsf T}b_{f_0}=0\).  Hence \(b_{f_0}\perp\ker G=\operatorname{range}(G)^\perp\), and therefore \(b_{f_0}\in\operatorname{range}G\).  Consequently
\[
E\{h(Qf_0)\mid X\}=b_{f_0}-GG^+b_{f_0}=0. \tag{29}
\]
Every coordinate of \(h=N_Bc\) belongs to \(\operatorname{range}N_B\), so \(Qf_0\) remains in that range.  Equations (26)--(29) and Theorem 2 imply \(Qf_0\in\mathcal T^\perp\).

It remains to verify the projection property.  For \(k\in\mathcal T^\perp\), pointwise \(D\)-orthogonality gives
\(E[((I-N_B)f_0)k\mid Y,X]=0\), while (28) gives
\[
E\{h^{\mathsf T}G^+b_{f_0}\,k\}
=E[(G^+b_{f_0})^{\mathsf T}E(hk\mid X)]=0.
\]
Therefore \(E\{(f_0-Qf_0)k\}=0\).  The range described by the three conditional-zero restrictions is an intersection of kernels of continuous conditional-expectation maps and is closed.  Hence \(Q\) is the \(L^2(P)\)-orthogonal projection onto \(\mathcal T^\perp\).  Cell positivity and the two Gram gaps bound the finite inverses; fixed rank makes the pseudoinverse Borel measurable, completing the integrability and measurability claims.
